prerequisites: Prior knowledge of signals and systems in continuous and discrete variables
Communication channels and analog and digital communication systems
Solid foundation in algebra and statistics

learning_outcomes.text: Know and understand the main mechanisms for encoding information in the form of a signal, regardless of its nature, efficiently and adapted to the problem under study.
Design mechanisms for sampling continuous signals and for efficient handling of the obtained samples, suitable for the characteristics of the information contained therein.
Conveniently manage information in the real domain and in transformed domains, continuous and discrete, as well as the relationships between the parameters that characterize these domains.
Analyze the information contained in deterministic and random signals, as well as their main properties.
Design and analyze equivalent analog and digital systems to process information represented in the form of a signal.
Design and analyze digital filters, both fixed and adaptive, according to the properties of the input and output signals, whether they are deterministic or random in nature.
Appropriately apply signal processing techniques for the implementation of different transmission and reception subsystems.
Know and use the main processing tools for voice, audio and image signals and the particularization of general signal processing tools to this type of information.
Know and conveniently use the terminology specific to signal treatment in communications and their processing, both in Spanish and English.
Argue and justify, orally and in writing, solutions adopted for communication problems based on signal processing techniques.

syllabus_topics: Continuous and discrete nature of information
Sampling of continuous signals: analysis in real and transformed domains
Modification of sampling rate through processing: decimation and interpolation
Systems for analog and digital processing
Representation of continuous systems using digital systems
Representation of digital systems using continuous systems
Definition of digital systems through difference equations
Impulse response, frequency response, and system function of a digital filter
Design and characterization of filters in the Z-domain
Analysis of the properties of deterministic signals in the real domain
Analysis of the properties of deterministic signals in transformed domains
Probabilistic tools for the study of random signals
Estimation of the properties of random signals
Calculation of optimal filters using normal equations
Iterative calculation of optimal filters: steepest descent algorithm
Transmission and reception subsystems based on signal processing
Processing in transmission and reception systems with spatial diversity
Other subsystems based on signal processing

assessment_methods.method: Final exam on problems and questions related to course content (Theory Block)
Practical evaluations (Practical Block) through three tests: sixth laboratory session, last laboratory session, fourth classroom practice session

assessment_rules: For ordinary and extraordinary calls, the final grade is calculated as: Theory Block grade (max 7 points) + Practical Block grade (max 3 points). The practical evaluation consists of three tests (10% each). In extraordinary calls, if the continuous practical evaluation is not obtained or not approved, it can be replaced by a practical exam. For differentiated evaluation, the practical block (30%) is assessed via a practical exam taken consecutively to the theoretical exam (70%).
